input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving

## Description

This epic runs the validation campaign that establishes first-hand functional
and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the platform's supported model
set on physical AMD Instinct accelerators, and produces the go/no-go scope for
productization. It resolves the strategy's central unknown — whether upstream
vLLM ROCm builds deliver acceptable parity for our supported models — which
determines the scope of the serving runtime productization work.

## Scope

- Stand up the validation environment on dedicated AMD Instinct nodes
  (procured or partner-lab access — see Risks), including the ROCm driver and
  runtime stack and the upstream vLLM ROCm builds.
- Execute a functional validation pass: serve each model in the supported
  model set under vLLM on ROCm, exercised through a KServe InferenceService
  (raw deployment or serverless mode), recording pass/fail per model.
- Execute a performance validation pass: measure serving throughput and
  latency per model on the AMD Instinct hardware against the CUDA baseline on
  comparable hardware.
- Produce the campaign report: per-model functional results, performance
  parity data, observed driver/runtime prerequisites, and a per-model go/no-go
  recommendation that defines the productization scope.
- Validate that KServe lifecycle and routing work unchanged on AMD GPU nodes
  (KServe requires no code changes; this confirmation is part of the campaign).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every model in the supported model set has a recorded functional
  pass/fail result for vLLM serving on ROCm, exercised through a KServe
  InferenceService.
- Every functionally-passing model has recorded throughput and latency
  measurements on AMD Instinct hardware, alongside the CUDA baseline
  measurements used for comparison.
- The campaign report delivers a per-model go/no-go recommendation that
  defines which models proceed to productization.
- The driver and runtime prerequisites observed on the AMD nodes are
  documented in the campaign report.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. This
  epic is the entirety of HLR-1.

## Risks

- **Hardware access is an availability precondition outside this strategy's
  control**: dedicated AMD Instinct nodes do not exist in the CI fleet, and
  procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved. This epic's work includes
  securing access, but the access being granted is not a condition the epic's
  deliverable produces — the campaign timeline depends on it.
- Upstream vLLM ROCm image releases are controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; the campaign pins available upstream builds and is not gated on
  release-train alignment.
- Re-split trigger: if the supported-model matrix exceeds a single campaign
  window, split into staged per-model-family campaign epics.

# Upstream ROCm image cadence assessment and base-image strategy

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's open question about upstream ROCm build
cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases and the upstream communities'
ROCm builds (vLLM serving images and PyTorch training images) align with the
platform's release trains. Its deliverable is a base-image strategy for all
productized ROCm runtimes — pin upstream images where cadence aligns, or build
from source with carried patches where it does not — which determines the
approach of the serving runtime productization and the PyTorch training
support work.

## Scope

- Collect the release history and cadence of AMD ROCm runtime releases and
  upstream vLLM / PyTorch ROCm image publications from public release records.
- Map that cadence against the platform's release train dates and support
  windows.
- Produce the base-image strategy: for each productized ROCm runtime (vLLM
  serving runtime, PyTorch training worker images), whether to pin an upstream
  image or build from source with patches, including the pinning and upgrade
  criteria.
- Record the misalignment scenarios and their mitigations (e.g. carrying
  patches, building from source, deferring a runtime to a later train) so the
  downstream implementation epics have a defined fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented cadence analysis maps AMD ROCm and upstream vLLM/PyTorch ROCm
  image release history against platform release train dates.
- A base-image strategy exists for each productized ROCm runtime, stating pin
  vs build-from-source with explicit selection criteria.
- Each misalignment scenario identified by the analysis carries a recorded
  mitigation that the downstream implementation epics can apply without
  re-opening the assessment.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: enables the productization of a supported vLLM ROCm serving
  runtime by selecting its base-image strategy (gating input, not direct
  scope).
- **HLR-3 (P1)**: enables PyTorch training on ROCm by selecting the PyTorch
  ROCm worker-image strategy (gating input, not direct scope).

## Risks

- AMD's release cadence is outside our control; the assessment documents and
  plans around it rather than changing it. If cadence fundamentally cannot
  support release trains, the fallback is the build-from-source strategy this
  epic selects.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the model set
the AMD Instinct validation campaign clears. It takes the vLLM ROCm build in
the existing midstream repository from an upstream-only capability to a
productized, supported runtime shipped for the platform, applying the
base-image strategy selected by the upstream ROCm cadence assessment.

## Scope

- Build the vLLM ROCm serving runtime image in the existing midstream vLLM
  repository, per the base-image strategy (pinned upstream ROCm base or
  build-from-source with patches).
- Productize the runtime as a supported serving runtime for the cleared model
  set (runtime distribution and support status — the platform currently ships
  only CUDA builds; ROCm builds exist upstream but are not shipped or
  supported).
- Verify serving of each cleared model on AMD Instinct hardware through a
  KServe InferenceService as part of bring-up.
- Wire the image build through the midstream Konflux pipeline (the pipeline
  onboarding work for the ROCm image variant runs in parallel — the coupling
  is enforced by the build-pipeline acceptance criterion below, not by a
  scheduling dependency).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm serving runtime image builds in the midstream repository for
  the model set cleared by the validation campaign.
- The ROCm image variant builds green in the midstream Konflux pipeline
  (build pipeline green).
- The runtime is productized with supported status for the cleared model set,
  applying the base-image strategy selected by the cadence assessment.
- Serving of each cleared model is verified on AMD Instinct hardware through
  a KServe InferenceService.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for
  the models the validation campaign clears. This epic is the entirety of
  HLR-2's productization scope (the build pipeline work is tracked separately
  as an enabler).

## Risks

- Scope is bounded by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome: if the
  campaign clears a smaller model set than the supported set, productization
  covers only the cleared models; if it clears none, productization is
  descoped to a future release and hardware access is revisited.
- Upstream ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD; if it misaligns with
  release trains, the fallback is the build-from-source strategy selected by
  the cadence assessment.
- Re-split trigger: split by model family if per-model bring-up exceeds the
  estimated volume and the epic outgrows a sprint.

# Konflux build pipeline for the vLLM ROCm image variant

## Description

This epic onboards the vLLM ROCm image variant onto the midstream Konflux
build pipeline. The vLLM midstream repository is already Konflux-onboarded
for its existing (CUDA) images; the ROCm variant is a new container image in
that existing repository and needs its own pipeline configuration. This work
runs in parallel with the runtime productization work — the coupling is
enforced by a build-pipeline-green acceptance criterion on the productization
work, not by a scheduling dependency.

## Scope

- Add Konflux pipeline configuration for the ROCm image variant in the
  existing midstream vLLM repository (new image, new base image, ROCm build
  recipe).
- Integrate the new pipeline with the repository's existing release machinery
  so the ROCm variant is built and released per platform version alongside
  the existing runtime images.
- Make the pipeline configuration accept the base-image selection as
  configuration (the pinned upstream ROCm base or build-from-source choice is
  filled in at execution time per the base-image strategy, and is not a
  scheduling dependency for this work).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Konflux pipeline configuration for the ROCm vLLM image variant exists in
  the midstream repository.
- The pipeline produces a green build of the ROCm image variant.
- The ROCm variant pipeline is integrated with the repository's existing
  release machinery (built and released per platform version).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: enables the productization of a supported vLLM ROCm serving
  runtime by providing its build pipeline (enabler; the repository is already
  Konflux-onboarded for existing images, so this covers the new image variant
  only).

## Risks

- ROCm builds may need build-host capabilities (ROCm toolchain) that the
  standard build environment lacks; if so, the pipeline configuration work
  includes provisioning the required build recipe.

# Kueue quota handling for amd.com/gpu

## Description

This epic adds amd.com/gpu quota handling to the platform's queueing layer so
that workloads requesting AMD GPUs are admitted with correct quota accounting.
It extends the existing ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model — already proven
for NVIDIA GPU resources — to the AMD GPU resource name, including gang
(all-or-nothing) admission semantics for multi-GPU jobs.

## Scope

- Define Kueue resource flavors and quota configuration covering
  amd.com/gpu (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue coverage for AMD GPU nodes), mirroring
  the existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling.
- Ensure all-or-nothing admission (waitForPodsReady gang semantics) applies
  correctly to workloads requesting amd.com/gpu, including multi-GPU jobs.
- Verify queueing behavior — pending/admitted workload accounting and quota
  enforcement — for amd.com/gpu workloads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Kueue quota configuration supports amd.com/gpu: a workload requesting
  amd.com/gpu is admitted against the correct quota and queue accounting is
  exposed as before.
- All-or-nothing admission is verified for multi-GPU jobs requesting
  amd.com/gpu (a job is admitted only when its full GPU allocation can be
  satisfied).
- Quota enforcement is demonstrated: a workload exceeding the configured
  amd.com/gpu quota remains pending rather than partially admitted.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling.
  This epic delivers the quota-handling half; the Training Operator job
  support is tracked separately (same HLR, different component).

## Risks

- Full end-to-end admission demonstration with running AMD GPU pods benefits
  from AMD Instinct nodes; quota accounting and admission semantics can be
  validated against the resource flavor configuration without them.

# PyTorch ROCm training support with Training Operator

## Description

This epic makes PyTorch training on ROCm a supported path for single- and
multi-GPU jobs run through the Training Operator, using PyTorch ROCm worker
images selected by the upstream cadence assessment's base-image strategy. It
extends the existing accelerated-training support — already proven for NVIDIA
GPUs — to AMD Instinct accelerators, with jobs admitted through the platform's
queueing layer using amd.com/gpu quota.

## Scope

- Support PyTorchJob single-GPU and multi-GPU (distributed) training jobs on
  ROCm: worker pods scheduled onto AMD GPU nodes requesting amd.com/gpu.
- Provide/select the PyTorch ROCm worker image per the base-image strategy
  chosen by the upstream ROCm cadence assessment (pinned upstream image or
  build-from-source with patches).
- Verify job admission through Kueue for amd.com/gpu workloads, including
  multi-GPU gang admission (the quota configuration itself is tracked as
  separate queueing-layer work; this epic verifies the end-to-end training
  path against it).
- Establish the supported status for the ROCm training path (single- and
  multi-GPU).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu runs to completion on AMD
  Instinct worker nodes with the selected PyTorch ROCm worker image.
- A multi-GPU (distributed) PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu runs to
  completion on AMD Instinct worker nodes.
- Multi-GPU jobs are admitted through Kueue with all-or-nothing semantics
  against amd.com/gpu quota.
- The PyTorch ROCm worker image strategy applied (pinned or built) matches the
  base-image strategy selected by the cadence assessment.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling.
  This epic delivers the Training Operator job-support half; the Kueue quota
  handling is tracked separately (same HLR, different component).

## Risks

- Validation on physical AMD Instinct nodes depends on hardware access

# Document AMD GPU (ROCm) support

## Description

This epic authors the customer-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm)
enablement: the supported AMD hardware, the driver prerequisites, and the
validated model list, covering both serving and training. It runs after the
implementations so the documentation describes what was actually built and
validated.

## Scope

Content outline (to be authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- **Supported AMD hardware**: the AMD Instinct accelerators supported for
  serving and training, as validated.
- **Driver prerequisites**: the ROCm driver and runtime prerequisites
  observed during the validation campaign and productization.
- **Validated model list**: the models cleared by the validation campaign and
  productized for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime.
- **Serving on ROCm**: using the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime,
  including deployment through KServe InferenceServices on AMD GPU nodes.
- **Training on ROCm**: single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJob training on AMD GPU
  nodes, including job admission through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota.
- **Base images**: the PyTorch ROCm worker image strategy and the vLLM ROCm
  runtime image, per the base-image strategy selected by the cadence
  assessment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the supported AMD hardware and the driver
  prerequisites.
- The documented validated model list matches the validation campaign's
  go/no-go outcome and the productized runtime's supported model set.
- The training documentation covers single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJob usage
  with Kueue admission and amd.com/gpu quota.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implementations (serving
  runtime, build pipeline, quota handling, and training support) before
  publication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list. This epic is the entirety of
  HLR-4.
